scope.blind_solve_method: candidate.json was read before editorial.json; answers below were recorded before seeing private option IDs.

source_access_limit: A licensed, searchable online text of Tolkien's original work/appendices was not accessible in this bounded review. The opened publisher page establishes the editions, but does not expose the passages. Tolkien Gateway and Tolkien File entries were opened only as secondary locators; they are not claimed as primary verification. An unaffiliated full-text PDF was reached but rejected as an authoritative source because provenance/rights were not established. Therefore direct-text citation locations are repair targets, and fact-certainty labels distinguish the limitation from the editorial verdict.

summary.key_parity: 12/12 blind answers matched the private keys
summary.primary_source_access: No licensed full original text opened; one original-person interview transcript endpoint was inaccessible and an accessible fan-site republication was treated as secondary.

items.fact_certainty: high for Lee/Saruman; medium for the annual-rereading attribution
findings: The casting answer is unique and distractors are comparable LOTR cast members.

The annual-reading claim is not tied to a named interview in the stem. The opened fan-site post attributes it to a Guardian interview, while the supplied explanation calls it a press-conference statement; those are not the same provenance.
The archival press-conference URL itself failed at robots retrieval, so it cannot support the claim in this review.
items.repair: Name and link the Guardian interview (or remove the annual-rereading clause); retain Lee as the key only after matching the explanation to that source.

items.fact_certainty: high, but direct primary-text access limited

items.blind_uncertainty: medium: Anduin is the intended late-Third-Age answer, but Sirion is also called the Great River in Tolkien's legendarium
items.fact_certainty: high that Anduin is called Great River; high that wording is ambiguous
findings: The opened secondary locator identifies Anduin as the Great River in Third-Age/Gondor usage.
Sirion, also offered as an option, is called the Great River in First-Age Beleriand. The unqualified phrase 'Великая река Средиземья' permits both, so the current single-choice key is not unique.
items.repair: Narrow the stem to 'Как называлась Великая река Гондора/Третьей Эпохи?' or remove Sirion; cite the relevant chapter/index entry.
items.source_status: secondary locator opened; direct primary-text access limited

items.fact_certainty: high, but direct primary-text access limited
findings: Gondor is the unique intended kingdom; distractors are peer Middle-earth regions/realms.
The wording does not say that Faramir and Boromir were kings, so it does not itself assert a false title.
items.repair: Add a precise canonical locator (The Return of the King/Appendix A).

items.blind_uncertainty: medium: Mithlond is the Grey Havens, but the question calls it a city and uses a loose location relation
items.fact_certainty: high for Mithlond/Grey Havens; medium for the exact wording
findings: Mithlond is the Sindarin name for the Grey Havens, the departure harbour associated with the White Ships.
'В каком городе находились' is imprecise: the text's setting is a haven/harbour, not a city label, and the phrase could imply that the ships were permanently located there.
items.repair: Ask 'Из какой гавани отплывали Белые Корабли?' and accept 'Митлонд (Серые Гавани)'; cite The Return of the King, 'The Grey Havens'.

items.fact_certainty: high for book event; medium for combined book/film formulation

The stem merges book and film without naming theatrical versus extended edition or a film scene. It also makes the keyed option conspicuously longer and more specific than every distractor, an answer cue.
items.repair: Ask only about The Return of the King book chapter 'The Last Debate'/'The Battle of the Pelennor Fields', or identify the exact film cut and scene. Replace choices with parallel ship descriptions of similar length.

items.fact_certainty: high for aran = king; high that the attribution is incomplete/misleading
findings: The word aran means 'king' in the relevant Elvish glossary tradition, and the options are parallel language terms.

'Elements in Quenya and Sindarin Names' is an appendix to The Silmarillion, not a standalone unqualified LOTR appendix. A Two Towers pack can ask it, but the source work must be named to avoid a false premise.
items.repair: Use 'В приложении к «Сильмариллиону» ...' or cite the correct LOTR appendix if a different source is intended; provide the exact edition/page.
